question: The correct karyotype notation for Turner syndrome is 45,XO, reflecting the absence of the second sex chromosome; SHOX gene haploinsufficiency on Xp22.3 is the principal cause of short stature in this condition.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. The karyotype is 45,X, NOT 45,XO. The 'O' suffix is an outdated informal convention; this notation error is a common and examinable mistake. The SHOX gene (short-stature homeobox gene) on Xp22.3 is indeed responsible for the short stature and skeletal features of Turner syndrome.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Actually, this statement is false. The correct notation is 45,X — the 'O' suffix (45,XO) is an outdated and incorrect convention; modern cytogenetics uses a 0 (zero) only informally and the standard ISCN notation is 45,X. The second part about SHOX is true — SHOX haploinsufficiency does cause the short stature and skeletal anomalies. The statement is false because of the karyotype notation error.
